summary: Attacked the restructuring proposal RS-29, which turns the proposed roadmap InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups into a Part II of the Tau Ceti roadmap BelyiMaps, narrows five of its seven layers, keeps two, and records 25 owner reassignments and 30 supplier links. No finding. The Part II title is an exact prefix extension of the parent's atlas title; every stage endpoint resolves; every owner genuinely owns the target it is given, checked in the owner's own text and down to four cited subsection numbers; the one library claim is exact at the pinned commit; every target of every narrowed layer is kept, moved or supplied, acceptance tests included; no consumer loses a prerequisite; the combined graph is acyclic; no Tau Ceti roadmap is changed; and the two layers left untouched duplicate nothing else in the atlas. The one surface that looked like a finding — ten owner entries naming BelyiMaps layers whose own text disclaims ownership in favour of successor roadmaps — is documented and deliberately chosen in RS-29.md, and is recorded below as checked rather than reported.
checked: The Part II title against PROTOCOL section 15. The parent's atlas title is 'Belyi maps, dessins d'enfants, and three-point covers' and the proposed title is exactly that followed by ', Part II: inverse Galois theory and arithmetic fundamental groups' — an exact prefix extension, not a paraphrase.

The choice of parent itself, since anchoring a general inverse-Galois roadmap on the three-point special case is the proposal's largest decision. It is supported by its own reassignments: 15 of the 25 owner entries move targets to BelyiMaps layers, so BelyiMaps is the dominant supplier rather than an arbitrary anchor.

Every stage endpoint in the file: all 25 owner entries, all 26 suppliedBy entries and all 30 links resolve to real atlas stage ids. The single exception is the sentinel UPSTREAM:Mathlib-Galois-category-classification, which is house practice — UPSTREAM: sentinels appear in nine accepted restructure result files, and this exact sentinel in four.

Whether every owner owns what it is said to. All 24 non-sentinel owner entries were matched term by term against the owner stage's title and description, and the six weakest or most load-bearing were read by hand. BelyiMaps layer 1 does carry the normalizer formulation, at its subsection 1.3, so 'Ordered passports and normalizer-orbit interpretation' is owned; BelyiMaps layer 6 classifies connected numbered covers by connected triples; PolynomialGaloisGroups layer 9 promises 'for every n >= 1 there is an explicit monic f : Z[X] of degree n, irreducible over Q, whose Galois action on the roots is the full symmetric group', which is the explicit S_n realization; and LocalFieldsRamification layer 2 proves Gal(K^ur/K) = Zhat with Zhat = lim Z/n, which is the 'Frobenius inverse-limit computation' assigned to it.

The four subsection citations the proposal makes by number, in BelyiMaps layer 12: 12.5 is 'The geometric fundamental group', defining pi_1^geo = Gal(Omega/Qbar(t)); 12.6 is 'The comparison isomorphism', pi_1^geo = profiniteCompletion (FreeGroup (Fin 2)); 12.8 is 'The arithmetic extension and the outer action', with the sequence 1 -> pi_1^geo -> Gal(Omega/Q(t)) -> Gal(Qbar/Q) -> 1; and 12.9 is 'Peripheral inertia, and the orientation of the comparison'. All four exist and say what IG.0's and IG.1's reasons say they say.

The one library claim, at the pinned commits (Mathlib 082e2d3, Tau Ceti f790474). The proposal's reason names 'PreGaloisCategory.functorToContAction and its IsEquivalence instance under GaloisCategory C and FiberFunctor F'. At the pin, Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Galois/Equivalence.lean declares functorToContAction at line 40 and the instance (functorToContAction F).IsEquivalence at line 90, both governed by the variable block [GaloisCategory C] [FiberFunctor F] at line 33. The claim is exact, including the hypotheses.

Whether every target of a changed layer is kept, moved or supplied. All seven IG stage descriptions were read in full and each Construction and Acceptance clause was matched against that layer's `keeps` text plus the owner entries whose `formerly` names it. Nothing is dropped, and the acceptance tests survive explicitly: IG.1 keeps the finite-field Frobenius and punctured-curve instances and the wild-inertia kernel with nontrivial examples; IG.3 keeps the dessin/triple comparison, the branch-cycle data check and the passport that does not determine the pair; IG.6 keeps the theorem-indexed solved-family list and marks the unrestricted inverse Galois problem over Q and generic-polynomial universality as frontier statements rather than inputs.

Whether any consumer loses a prerequisite. The seven IG stages have exactly nine recorded consumer edges, which is the number RS-29.md claims to preserve. The one outside consumer that narrowing could have stranded is ArithmeticDynamics:DY.5, a consumer of IG.0, and it is given its own direct supplier edge from ModularCurves 0d rather than being left to a narrowed IG.0; AnabelianGeometryAndNonabelianChabauty:NC.0, the outside consumer of IG.1, receives edges from IG.0 and from BelyiMaps layer 12.

Cycles, on the graph that matters rather than on the new links alone. There is no cycle among the 30 links, and none in the combined graph of the atlas's 3458 existing stage edges together with the 29 non-sentinel links. The existing graph was acyclic too, so the proposal introduces none. In particular the new NC.0 -> IG.6 edge is safe: NC.0 depends on IG.1, and IG.6 is downstream of IG.1 through IG.2 to IG.5.

That no Tau Ceti roadmap is changed. The `layers` dictionary contains only the seven InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups stage ids; no Tau Ceti layer is narrowed, kept or otherwise acted on. The targets assigned to Tau Ceti layers are ones those layers already contain, which is the owner check above, so this is import rather than re-planning.

Duplication left standing in the two layers the proposal does not narrow, IG.2 and IG.5, since a restructuring proposal that misses one has failed at its own job. Searching every roadmap in the atlas: Hilbert irreducibility occurs in no other roadmap, and Hurwitz moduli in no other roadmap; AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.4, which IG.5 depends on, is general algebraic-stack theory with no Hurwitz content. IG.4's retained Shafarevich solvable realization theorem is not duplicated by ProfiniteProPGroups layer 5 either: that layer's only Shafarevich is the Golod-Shafarevich inequality, and it contains no realization statement at all, which is what the proposal's reason asserts.

The surface that most looked like a finding, and why it is not reported as one. BelyiMaps layers 7 to 14 each open with '**Owner:** successor roadmap `BelyiAnalyticCovers`' (or `BelyiAlgebraicAndDescent`, or `BelyiArithmeticActions`), followed by 'Retained here as a dependency specification; no milestone of this layer is a declaration or a completion claim'. Ten of the 25 owner entries and twelve of the 30 links land on those disclaimed layers. Three things clear it: none of the three successors exists as an atlas roadmap or stage, so there is no id to point at; RS-29.md states the situation and the choice outright — 'These are ownership contracts in that document. They are not substituted with invented atlas stage IDs: the JSON uses the existing tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/BelyiMaps#layer-... IDs that retain those contracts', and 'Their absence as separate atlas stages is recorded here, not repaired by creating phantom IDs'; and the owner schema (target, owner, formerly) has no field in which a successor contract could be recorded. The dependency risk is real but pre-existing, since IG.3's own stage text already said to consume those successors.

The proposal's own self-validation claims, since a proposal that miscounts its own checks is worth doubting. The family evidence file research/blueprint/restructure/RS-29.json lists exactly 15 evidence pairs, and every one of the 15 is represented by a supplier link or a suppliedBy entry; the nine consumer edges it claims to preserve are exactly the nine the atlas records for the seven IG stages.
